The '''2022 Richmond upon Thames London Borough Council election''' took place on 5 May 2022. All 54 members of [[Richmond upon Thames London Borough Council]] were elected. The elections took place alongside [[2022 London local elections|local elections in the other London boroughs]] and [[2022 United Kingdom local elections|elections to local authorities across the United Kingdom]].

The 2022 election took place under new election boundaries, with the number of councillors remaining the same. The [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] had controlled the council since the [[2018 Richmond upon Thames London Borough Council election|previous election in 2018]], and increased their majority, ending on 48 seats, with all Liberal Democrat candidates being elected.{{Efn|Opposition councillors were elected only in wards where there were not as many Liberal Democrat candidates as seats available for that ward.}} The [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] formed the largest opposition group on five seats, with the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] dropping from 11 seats to 1 seat; they would subsequently lose their final seat in a 2024 by-election.

== Background ==
=== History ===
The thirty-two [[London boroughs]] were established in 1965 by the [[London Government Act 1963]]. They are the principal authorities in Greater London and have responsibilities including education, housing, planning, highways, social services, libraries, recreation, waste, environmental health and revenue collection. Some of the powers are shared with the [[Greater London Authority]], which also manages passenger transport, police and fire.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The essential guide to London local government {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/essential-guide-london-local-government|access-date=2021-10-10|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref>

Since its formation, Richmond upon Thames has been under [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] control, [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrat]] control, [[SDP–Liberal Alliance]] control and [[no overall control]]. The Liberal Democrats regained control from the Conservatives in the [[2018 Richmond upon Thames London Borough Council election|most recent election in 2018]]. They won 39 seats with 46.7% of the vote across the borough while the Conservatives won 11 seats with 37.6% of the vote and the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Greens]] won 4.5% of the vote. The [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] won 10.4% of the vote but did not win any seats.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Blunden|first=Mark|date=2018-05-04|title=Lib Dems seize Richmond from the Conservatives|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/local-election-2018-liberal-democrats-seize-richmonduponthames-from-the-conservatives-a3830906.html|access-date=2021-10-20|website=www.standard.co.uk|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Holder|first=Josh|title=Local council elections 2018 – results in full|url=http://www.theguardian.com/politics/ng-interactive018/may/04/local-council-election-results-2018-in-full|access-date=2021-10-19|website=the Guardian|language=en}}</ref> The leader of the Liberal Democrat group, Gareth Roberts, became council leader following the election.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Election results: Leader of Liberal Democrats promises fresh start for borough|url=https://www.richmondandtwickenhamtimes.co.uk/news/16211405.election-results-leader-liberal-democrats-promises-fresh-start-borough/|access-date=2021-10-20|website=Richmond and Twickenham Times|date=8 May 2018 |language=en}}</ref>

=== Council term ===

In 2019, Mona Adams, the Liberal Democrat councillor for [[East Sheen]], died.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Adams|first=Bernard|date=2019-09-18|title=Mona Adams obituary|url=http://www.theguardian.com/media/2019/sep/18/mona-adams-obituary|access-date=2021-10-20|website=the Guardian|language=en}}</ref> A by-election was held to fill her seat on 19 July 2019, which was won by the Liberal Democrat candidate Julia Cambridge.<ref>{{Cite web|title=East Sheen Ward by-election 2019|url=https://www.richmond.gov.uk/council/elections_voting_and_registration/elections_and_referendums/election_results/local_election_results/east_sheen_ward_by_election|access-date=2021-10-20|website=London Borough of Richmond upon Thames|language=en-gb}}</ref> Cambridge was a designer who had unsuccessfully contested the seat alongside Adams in the 2018 election.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Meet the East Sheen by-election hopefuls who want to represent the area|url=https://www.richmondandtwickenhamtimes.co.uk/news/17749443.meet-east-sheen-by-election-hopefuls-want-represent-area/|access-date=2021-10-20|website=Richmond and Twickenham Times|date=4 July 2019 |language=en}}</ref> In July 2020, Dylan Bexendale, the Green Party councillor for Hampton Wick, resigned citing personal reasons.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Reporter|first=Sian Bayley, Local Democracy|title=Green Party councillor resigns but cannot be replaced until May 2021|url=https://richmond.nub.news/n/green-party-councillor-resigns-but-cannot-be-replaced-until-may-2021|access-date=2021-10-20|website=richmond.nub.news|date=July 2020 |language=en}}</ref> Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], a by-election to fill his seat could not be held until 6 May 2021 alongside the [[2021 London mayoral election]] and [[2021 London Assembly election|London Assembly election]]. The election was won by the Liberal Democrat candidate Petra Fleming.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-05-10|title=Lewis Baston: Swings to Tories but comfort for Labour in 'Super Thursday' borough by-elections|url=https://www.onlondon.co.uk/lewis-baston-swings-to-tories-but-comfort-for-labour-in-super-thursday-borough-by-elections/|access-date=2021-10-20|website=OnLondon|language=en-GB}}</ref>

As with most London boroughs, Richmond upon Thames was electing its councillors under new boundaries decided by the [[Local Government Boundary Commission for England]], which it produced after a period of consultation. The number of councillors remained at 54, but the commission produced new boundaries following a period of consultation, with eighteen three-member wards.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Local Government Boundary Commission for England Consultation Portal|url=https://consultation.lgbce.org.uk/node/16793|access-date=2021-10-20|website=consultation.lgbce.org.uk}}</ref>

== Electoral process ==
Richmond upon Thames, like other London borough councils, elects all of its councillors at once every four years. The previous election took place in 2018. The election took place by [[block voting]], with each ward being represented by two or three councillors. Electors had as many votes as there are councillors to be elected in their ward, with the top two or three being elected.

All [[Elections in the United Kingdom#Registration procedure|registered electors]] ([[British citizen|British]], [[Irish citizen|Irish]], [[Commonwealth citizen|Commonwealth]] and [[European Union]] citizens) living in London aged 18 or over were entitled to vote in the election. People who live at two addresses in different councils, such as university students with different term-time and holiday addresses, were entitled to be registered for and vote in elections in both local authorities.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=How the elections work {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/london-elections/how-elections-work|access-date=2021-09-14|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref> Voting in-person at polling stations took place from 7:00 to 22:00 on election day, and voters were able to apply for postal votes or proxy votes in advance of the election.<ref name=":1" />
